refnamediv.refpurpose: Inspect the platform-authentication state and produce attestation

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: trustctl inspects the platform-authentication state maintained by platformd-trustd.service8, evaluates its policies, and produces attestation. It is a client of the io.platformd.Trust varlink7 interface; the reading commands require no privilege, while the attestation commands (attest, attest-token, enroll, activate-credential) must run as root. The daemon restricts evidence production because it is a signing operation on the shared TPM. provision and remove-boot-reference require privilege to update boot references. verify-attestation verifies supplied evidence offline and requires neither privilege, a running daemon, nor a TPM.

listitem.para: Show the boot evidence and a summary of the platform-authentication state.
List the tracked login sessions with their lock and verification state.
Show the record for the session ID, including the identity behind it and whether that identity is verified.

Evaluate POLICY for the session ID and print the result, stable reason code, descriptive reason, and freshness window. The policies are verified-boot, fresh-user-verification, and local-trusted-session. The result is policy-satisfied or denied.
Show the recorded authentication events, most recent first, and whether each event established verification freshness.
Show the measured-boot PCRs of the SHA-256 bank and the boot grade.

Show the runtime authentication measurement log: the authentication, lock, and sleep state events folded into the extend-only TPM NV index, with the baseline and current values needed to replay it. Version 2 extends the SHA-256 digest of each serialized record. Its boot ID, timestamps, provenance, and payload are included in that digest.

Produce a TPM quote over the boot PCRs, bound to NONCE (a hexadecimal string). If none is given a random nonce is generated. The quote is verifiable against the attestation key's public part without trusting the service.

Produce a platformd-specific JSON evidence envelope containing the TPM quote, boot measurements, and runtime log. Only the embedded TPM structures are signed; local assertions are unsigned. The envelope is not an IETF Entity Attestation Token.

Verify a version 2 platformd attestation envelope against an independently supplied Attestation Key and challenge. The key file contains the hexadecimal marshaled TPM2B_PUBLIC, with optional surrounding whitespace. Both inputs must be regular files; the envelope is limited to 16 MiB and the key file to 4096 bytes. The challenge is required and must contain 1 through 64 bytes encoded as hexadecimal.

Verify the quote and NV certification signatures, challenge, signer and TPM lifecycle, quoted PCR digest, NV definition and value, and exact runtime-log replay. Print the successful checks and retained event count as JSON. No result is printed when verification fails.

Success establishes evidence integrity under the supplied key. It does not establish key enrollment, approved boot state, complete boot history, trusted timestamps, authentication freshness, or access authorization. Local assertions remain unsigned. An empty retained runtime log is valid only when its baseline equals the certified value; it contains no authentication evidence. The requester must generate, expire, and consume its challenges. Reusing a challenge is not detected by this command.
Show the enrollment evidence: the Endorsement Key public key and, when present, its manufacturer certificate, together with the Attestation Key public key and TPM name.

Complete a credential-activation challenge, given the credential blob and encrypted secret produced by a verifier's TPM2_MakeCredential (both hexadecimal). The challenge is recovered only if the attestation key and the Endorsement Key are resident together. The verifier must independently establish trust in the Endorsement Key; credential activation alone does not establish manufacturer provenance.

Compute the expected boot measurement from the sections of the unified kernel image UKI, using systemd-measure1, and record it for one boot entry. REFERENCE-ID defaults to the UKI filename. This is normally run by the kernel-install8 plugin on each kernel installation.
Remove the reference for one boot entry. The kernel-install8 plugin uses this when removing a kernel.
Print a short help text and exit.

refsect1.title: Exit status
refsect1.para: On success 0 is returned, a non-zero failure code otherwise.

listitem.para: The directory holding the io.platformd.Trust socket. Defaults to /run/platformd-trustd.
